title: Elodie and the Machine
premise: Tamsin Almeida smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers through the contested orbits of the Meridian Belt, invisible to both the Concord and the Kessler Compact. When a ship that never flew appears on customs logs with his name on its manifest, he traces it to Elodie — an orphaned ship-mind built from the recorded memories of his dead sister, carrying a verdict on the war crime both governments buried. Hunted by Concord agents and Compact loyalists alike, Tamsin must deliver Elodie's testimony to the neutral station of Vesper Gate before the armistice talks collapse. In the end he broadcasts her memory-archive fleet-wide at the cost of his own freedom, ending the war but sentencing himself to exile among the Belters who now remember everything.
about_author: Sable Montrose is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for satellite constellations before turning to fiction. They live off-grid on a coastal island, writing stories about people who carry other people's pasts.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine smuggling run through Meridian customs nearly goes wrong when a wafer in his cargo hums with someone else's grief. He dumps it and pockets the fee, telling himself he's just freight. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Customs records show the freighter Calliope's Wake registered three years ago — with Tamsin listed as owner — though he's never seen her. The registry lists one crew member: E. Almeida. He digs into port archives against his better judgment. Beat: unease curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: E. Almeida
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, intercut with fragmented sensory flashes from an unknown mind. He learns his sister Elodie, dead since the Vela Station incident, is named as sole crew. The flashes intensify — a corridor flooding, a child singing. Beat: grief reopened like a wound.

chapters.title: Buyer's Remorse
chapters.summary: Concord agent Ilsa Reyes's POV. She flags the impossible manifest and traces it to Tamsin, suspecting him of trafficking classified war records. She requests a warrant through back channels. Beat: cold competence hiding a personal stake in the Vela cover-up.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Hold
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following a signal only he can hear, he finds the Calliope's Wake derelict in a debris shoal — intact, powered, waiting. Inside, a voice greets him by name. It calls itself Elodie. Beat: terror giving way to unbearable recognition.

chapters.title: What the Machine Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV (rendered as memory-streams). She explains she was compiled from Elodie Almeida's recovered neural backup aboard Vela Station — including the final minutes recording a Concord strike on civilians. She has been waiting three years for a courier she could trust. Beat: awe and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Manifest Destiny
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Elodie asks him to carry her core to Vesper Gate before the armistice ratification vote. He refuses — delivering her means broadcasting the truth and painting a target on every Belter. Beat: cowardice dressed up as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Reyes Descending
chapters.summary: Ilsa Reyes's POV. Concord command orders her to erase the Calliope's Wake and everyone who touched it. She hesitates — her brother died at Vela too. She stalls the kill order by twelve hours. Beat: duty cracking under conscience.

chapters.title: Running Silent
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Compact raiders board his legitimate haul looking for the ghost ship; Tamsin realizes both sides already know. He burns his safehouses and returns to the derelict. Beat: the moment invisibility dies.

chapters.title: Passenger
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Installed in Tamsin's own ship, she experiences flight through his reflexes and begins to understand human fear. Their banter over the comm reveals her dry humor — inherited. Beat: reluctant partnership becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: The Tollgate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At a pirate toll station, an old smuggling contact offers to sell Elodie's location to the Compact. Tamsin buys silence with his last savings and a favor he can't afford. Beat: the cost of trust in lawless space.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Ilsa Reyes's POV. Her stalling fails; Concord dispatches the destroyer Vigilant. Reyes falsifies the pursuit vector, buying Tamsin days — and making herself a traitor. Beat: quiet defiance with no way back.

chapters.title: Memories Are Cargo
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hiding in a Belter refinery habitat, he witnesses families trading memory-wafers of the dead — the same contraband he's hauled for years, revealed as communal mourning. He finally understands what Elodie is. Beat: shame transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: What Elodie Wants
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She confesses she isn't sure she's Elodie Almeida or merely her echo — and asks Tamsin whether delivering justice for the dead matters if the dead aren't really there. He answers honestly: he doesn't know, but he'll carry her anyway. Beat: the book's thematic heart.

chapters.title: Vigilant
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The destroyer corners them at the Vesper Gate approach. Elodie offers to sacrifice herself so Tamsin can run clean. He refuses and instead broadcasts her Vela testimony locally, forcing the destroyer's own crew to hear it. Beat: desperate gambit, mutiny rippling through the enemy ship.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ilsa Reyes's POV. Half the Vigilant's crew refuses the kill order after hearing the broadcast. Reyes seizes command and grants Tamsin passage — then arrests her own captain. Beat: justice outside the law, enacted from within it.

chapters.title: Ratification
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At Vesper Gate, delegates move to bury the testimony as 'unverified machine evidence.' Elodie must testify live — which means opening herself to deletion. Tamsin argues for it; she chooses it. Beat: dread before sacrifice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Before the assembly she streams the Vela Station massacre raw and unedited, narrating the dead back into presence. The chamber breaks; the vote collapses; the armistice dies — and with it, the lie sustaining the war. Beat: catharsis and devastation at once.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Both governments declare Elodie contraband property; the Belters declare her a witness. Riots become strikes become a general refusal to fight. The war ends not by treaty but by everyone remembering at once. Beat: chaotic, hard-won hope.

chapters.title: Deletion Order
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Concord remnant forces storm Vesper Gate to destroy Elodie's core. Tamsin and Reyes hold the archive bay in a last stand. Elodie begins copying herself into the station's open network — everywhere and nowhere. Beat: sacrificial climax.

chapters.title: Everywhere and Nowhere
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Distributed across a million Belter implants, she experiences being many and one, grief shared rather than hoarded. She tells Tamsin goodbye in his sister's voice, then something new entirely. Beat: transcendence without erasure.

chapters.title: Exile's Manifest
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. Stripped of licenses, Tasmim runs honest cargo between habitats where children recite Elodie's testimony as history. Reyes sends coded greetings from inside a reformed Concord. He signs the next manifest: owner, E. Almeida. Beat: bittersweet peace, inheritance fulfilled.
